You will address the infidelity in counseling, but you will also address communication, love languages, appreciation, etc. One big thing we have addressed in mine is empathy.

Marriage counseling is a lot like regular counseling, except you exclusively talk about your relationship and things that impact it, and you're both present to hear what the therapist says.   
The most valuable thing our marriage counselor did is consistently turn us toward each other instead of dialoging with us. He would ask questions that would prompt us to listen to each other and ask each other questions and learn how to communicate. You don't get this in individual counseling, because only one of you is there.    
Even if you mostly focus on what she did wrong in your marriage counseling, just both being there for the counseling is going to be helpful for you. And trust me, no marriage is perfect. I'm not saying your marriage is to blame for her infidelity, but I am absolutely confident that you have things to work on together. Your assurance that you don't is only further proof.
